frozen_decisions_applied: S4 MQTT required change #13: subscribe_command_topics() subscribes only to the v1 DeviceId-keyed wildcards; the legacy short-address wildcards are never subscribed in production. The legacy parse/dispatch code stays in the binary (reachable directly for host tests/dev use, matching the HTTP v1 precedent of keeping-but-not-registering legacy paths) but is unreachable via a real broker once nothing subscribes it.

S4 MQTT required change #14 (partial, deliberately): a one-time (per boot), idempotent retained-empty-payload tombstone sweep runs on the first sync after start() for the 3 per-device legacy topics (state/telemetry/availability) of every device active at that moment. The HA-discovery portion of #14 is deliberately deferred alongside #16-#19 -- see deviations.

S4 MQTT required change #15: the device-sync diff cache is now keyed by DeviceId (device_id_hex) instead of short_addr, so a short_addr remap is recognized as the same device rather than a disappearance+recreation. This is the actual mechanism that guarantees a remap never touches a legacy topic again after cutover (the tombstone sweep only ever fires once, on the very first sync, regardless of any later remap).

FD-01/FD-03 applied to MQTT command ingress for the first time: an MQTT v1 command for an unresolvable device_id is rejected outright (via ServiceRuntimeApi::resolve_short_addr_for_device_id_hex(), the same golden-matrix-adjacent API HTTP v1 already uses), never silently written under a synthetic/guessed identity.

INV-M026 (mqtt_bridge adapters must not name core:: symbols) satisfied via the same auto-typed resolve_device_id_for_short_addr() pattern already established for the legacy handler and for HTTP v1's reporting-profile write; common::GatewayId is named directly (INV-M026 does not restrict common::, only core::), consistent with the foundation pass's own documented reasoning.

command_subscription_cutover.detail: subscribe_command_topics() now calls hal_mqtt_subscribe() with topic_v1_device_config_set_wildcard()/topic_v1_device_power_set_wildcard() instead of the legacy equivalents -- the literal, complete implementation of plan #13. Verified by grep (the legacy topic_device_config_wildcard()/topic_device_power_set_wildcard() calls no longer appear in subscribe_command_topics()) and by the new v1 command tests in test_mqtt_bridge_commands.cpp/test_application_command_mapper.cpp.

outbound_publishing_cutover.detail: mqtt_device_sync.cpp's sync_snapshot() and mqtt_bridge.cpp's sync_device_state() publish exclusively to v1 topics for live content (availability/state/telemetry) from this pass onward; the diff cache that decides what changed is keyed by device_id_hex, not short_addr. A device with no resolved identity yet is tracked but generates no v1 publications until it resolves. Tested via test_mqtt_device_sync.cpp's full rewrite and test_mqtt_runtime_feed.cpp's rewrite through the real ServiceRuntime path.

remap_safety.detail: The device_id_hex-keyed diff cache means a short_addr remap of an already-known device produces zero publications (no availability flicker, and -- critically -- no legacy topic is ever touched for the device's new short_addr, satisfying plan #15's literal text). Directly tested: test_mqtt_device_sync.cpp's remap test asserts sync_snapshot() returns 0 for a snapshot that only changes an already-cached device's short_addr.

legacy_tombstone_sweep.status: COMPLETE, TESTED, DELIBERATELY PARTIAL (per-device topics only, not HA discovery)
legacy_tombstone_sweep.detail: build_legacy_tombstone_publication() publishes a retained empty payload to each active device's 3 legacy topics (state/telemetry/availability), gated to fire only on the very first sync_snapshot() call after start()/reset_sync_cache() (cache_initialized_ false->true transition). Publishing the same empty payload again on a later boot remains idempotent by ordinary MQTT retained-message semantics. Tested: test_mqtt_device_sync.cpp asserts exactly 6 publications (3 v1 + 3 tombstones) on the first sync, 0 extra tombstones on the second sync for an unchanged device, and that a device whose identity resolves only on a *later* sync still gets its one-time tombstone on the sync where it first appears active (not retroactively, not repeated).

ha_discovery_tombstone_deferred.detail: Plan #14's text names 'HA discovery topics' alongside state/availability/telemetry as things to tombstone during the upgrade. This pass does not tombstone legacy HA discovery topics, because doing so without also publishing v1-based discovery (plan #16-#19, unstarted) would delete the operator's real Home Assistant entities with nothing to replace them -- a functional regression on a live system, not a reviewed migration. mqtt_discovery.cpp is completely unmodified by this pass.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Plan #14's HA-discovery-topic tombstoning is not implemented in this pass; only the 3 per-device legacy topics (state/telemetry/availability) are tombstoned.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: The plan's own cutover-order section (Stage S4, 'Migration, compatibility and rollout behavior', steps 4-5) places tombstoning old HA discovery immediately before publishing new v1 discovery -- the two are meant to happen together, in the same transition window. Tombstoning HA discovery now, with plan #16-#19 (the v1 discovery replacement) entirely unimplemented, would delete the operator's real Home Assistant entities and publish nothing to replace them: a genuine functional regression on a system this plan's own FD/invariant language treats as already running in production (main/app_main.cpp already starts MqttBridge unconditionally today), not a defensible reading of 'during upgrade.'
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: Legacy HA discovery entities remain exactly as they were before this pass; Home Assistant continues to show them, driven by the legacy short_addr-keyed state/availability topics this pass's tombstone sweep just wiped. This is itself a real interaction to be aware of before this firmware is ever built and flashed: once flashed, any device active at that moment gets its legacy state/availability/telemetry retained messages cleared, but its HA discovery config (which points at those now-empty legacy topics) is left in place and unreplaced until #16-#19 lands -- meaning that device's HA entities would go stale/unavailable in the operator's dashboard until the HA migration pass completes. This is the direct, load-bearing reason #16-#19 is now the explicit next step, not an optional follow-up.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: No new architecture-gate rule was added to enforce that production topic subscriptions stay v1-only going forward (no equivalent of INV-H010 for 'must not subscribe legacy wildcards').
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Unlike HTTP v1's registration functions (a single named call site that could be reintroduced accidentally), subscribe_command_topics() is one function with an inline, directly-readable pair of hal_mqtt_subscribe() calls; a grep-based invariant naming the legacy topic constants would be straightforward to add but was judged lower priority than the substantial functional-behavior work this pass already covers with direct tests (subscribe_command_topics() itself is exercised implicitly through the ESP_PLATFORM-gated code path, which the host/sanitizer suite cannot compile or run at all -- see unresolved_blockers).
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A future edit could reintroduce a legacy hal_mqtt_subscribe() call to subscribe_command_topics() without any automated check catching it before real hardware. This is an explicit, named gap for a future pass to close, not an oversight.
